lines.text: Pick to stone, drill to crystal. Power must meet hardness, lad. Else the rock just laughs.
Swing smart. Stamina’s a keg—sip, don’t gulp. Rest a breath after a flurry.
Workbench, then forge, then steam works. Copper first, iron next, and the drill sings last.
Copper likes bright lanes—veins near worked stone. Listen for a hollow ring in your swing.
Iron won’t yield to a basic pick. Reinforce your bite or waste your sweat.
Hold the drill steady—spin up, bite, cool down. Don’t nurse it on soft wall; save teeth for ore.
Three‑Wide Law keeps us breathing. Doors in threes, lanes in threes. Stone respects a measured march.
The First Warrant ended clan squabbles here. Lamps at doors mark safe mouths of the stone.
Goblins telegraph like drunk fiddlers—hear the tune, raise your block, and they hush quick.
Mind the floor hum—burrowers burst from below. Step aside or let your shield kiss their snout.
